Consult Summary:
- Patient presents with a severe, persistent headache for three days with visual disturbances, not fully relieved by analgesia; migraine suspected, examination and further evaluation advised.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe, "blinding" headache ongoing for three days.
- Onset: Sudden onset upon awakening three days prior.
- Duration: Persistent, continuously present over three days.
- Severity: Rated 8/10 at worst, improves to 5/10 with Ibuprofen but never resolves fully.
- Location: Diffuse, but more intense over the right eye.
- Progression: Ongoing; not improving significantly with current medications.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Slight improvement with Ibuprofen; worsens with sudden standing or head movement.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Photophobia (increased sensitivity to light).
  - Visual disturbance described as "shooting light" and "weird kind of vision."
  - Mild nausea but no vomiting.
  - No aura, no prior similar severe headaches.
  - No past headaches with visual symptoms, nausea, or vomiting.
  - No recent fevers, weight change, respiratory or sinus symptoms, or changes in smell/taste.
  - No focal neurological symptoms (no tingling, numbness, or weakness).
  - Normal sleep; not waking at night from headache.
  - Fatigue attributed to headaches, affecting ability to work.
- Functional impact: Unable to focus or perform usual work-from-home tasks; missed part/all of workdays over last three days.
- Negative findings: No nasal bleeds, no cough or hemoptysis, no night awakening with headache.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic illnesses reported.
- Childhood episode of pain (not specified), no underlying cause found, resolved.

Medications:
- Oral contraceptive pill (specific name not documented), ongoing for one year, dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Ibuprofen used as needed for headache, dose/route/frequency not documented.
- No side effects from oral contraceptive reported.
- No noted increase in headache frequency since starting oral contraceptive.
- No other regular medications.
- Allergies: None reported.

Social History:
- Lives alone.
- Non-smoker.
- Drinks alcohol regularly, approximately once per week.
- No recreational drug use reported.
- Works from home; recent headaches have impacted ability to work.

Family History:
- Mother has migraines with vomiting.
- No other relevant family medical history reported.

Physical Examination:
- No findings documented (remote consult, no examination possible).

Investigations:
- Recent eye check: no changes noted.
- Blood pressure last measured one year ago (when starting oral contraceptive), reported as normal.
- No other investigations or test results provided.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Persistent severe headache with visual disturbance; possible migraine.
  - Plan:
    - Book in-person appointment for full neurological and fundoscopic examination (including blood pressure check).
    - Medication: Prescribe analgesic stronger than Ibuprofen; instruct patient to take with food. Advise Paracetamol may be used in addition as needed.
    - Counselled on signs of worsening (increased severity, change in symptoms, functional decline): advised to seek immediate care at emergency department if occurs.
    - Advise to continue current oral contraceptive for now; to be reassessed pending full evaluation due to potential contraindication in migraine with aura.
- Issue 2: Impact of headache on daily functioning and work.
  - Plan: Support time off as needed until further assessment; monitor for improvement or worsening.
- Issue 3: Family history of migraine.
  - Plan: Noted for consideration in diagnosis and future management.

General Plan:
- Patient to arrange appointment with clinic for in-person assessment.
- Referral to specialist may be considered depending on in-person findings.
- Patient advised to call clinic for further advice or if symptoms worsen before appointment.

Quality checks:

●	Missing elements: 
  - Vital signs, objective physical exam findings, and comprehensive medication list (with doses/frequency) not available.
  - No direct documentation of temperature measurement.
  - No urinalysis, labs, or neuroimaging performed/documented at this consult.
●	Conflict: None noted.
●	Transcript quality: Audio at start was difficult due to volume and possible patient name and details not captured; overall, clinical details clearly documented from history.
